historical_references.reference: In medieval folklore, Thalassina was a sea nymph or mermaid associated with the Adriatic Sea. The name Thalassina comes from the Greek 'thalassa' meaning sea.
historical_references.context: Thalassina was believed to help sailors navigate the treacherous waters of the Adriatic Sea and protect them from storms and pirates.

historical_references.reference: According to Greek mythology, Thalassina was the daughter of Poseidon, the god of the sea, and Amphitrite, the goddess of the sea. She was one of the Nereids, sea nymphs who attended to Poseidon and the sea.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient Greece (8th century BC to 146 BC)
historical_references.context: Thalassina and the other Nereids were believed to have the power to control the sea and weather, and were often depicted as beautiful and graceful figures.
